{{Nihongo|'''Yoshinori Ohsumi'''|大隅 良典|Ōsumi Yoshinori|extra=born February 9, 1945}} is a Japanese [[cell biology|cell biologist]] specializing in [[autophagy]], the process that cells use to destroy and recycle cellular components.

Ohsumi is a professor at [[Institute of Science Tokyo]]'s Institute of Innovative Research.<ref name="orcid">Yoshinori Ohsumi's {{ORCID|0000-0003-2384-2166}}</ref> He received the [[Kyoto Prize]] for Basic Sciences in 2012,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://chronicle.com/blogs/ticker/kyoto-prize-is-awarded-to-3-scholars/51696?cid=gn|title=Kyoto Prize Is Awarded to 3 Scholars|last=Biemiller|first=Lawrence|date=November 10, 2012|website=The Chronicle of Higher Education Blogs: The Ticker|access-date=October 4, 2016}}</ref> the 2016 [[Nobel Prize]] in [[Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine|Physiology or Medicine]], and the 2017 [[Breakthrough Prize]] in Life Sciences<ref name="Breakthrough2017">{{cite web|title=Laureates—Breakthrough Prize|url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/2|website=Breakthrough Prize|access-date=December 5, 2016}}</ref> for his discoveries of mechanisms for [[autophagy]].<ref name="nobelprize">{{cite web|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/medicine/laureates/2016/press.html |title=The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2016 |publisher=The Nobel Foundation |date=October 3, 2016 |access-date=October 3, 2016}}</ref>

== Biography ==
[[File:Yoshinori Osumi 20151029.jpg|thumb|Ohsumi addressed at [[Gairdner Foundation International Award]] Ceremony (at the [[Royal Ontario Museum]] in October 2015)]]
[[File:John Dirks Yoshinori Osumi Kenjiro Monji and D Lorne Tyrrell 20151029.jpg|thumb|with [[John Dirks (physician)|John Dirks]], Kenjirō Monji and [[D. Lorne Tyrrell]] ]]

Ohsumi was born on February 9, 1945, in [[Fukuoka]]. He received a [[B.Sci.]] in 1967 and a D.Sci. in 1974, both from the [[University of Tokyo]]. In 1974–77 he was a [[postdoctoral fellow]] at the [[Rockefeller University]] in New York City.<ref name=orcid />

He returned to the University of Tokyo in 1977 as a [[research associate]]; he was appointed Lecturer there in 1986, and promoted to Associate Professor in 1988. In 1996, he moved to the [[National Institute for Basic Biology, Japan]] in [[Okazaki City]], where he was appointed as a professor. From 2004 to 2009, he was also professor at the [[Graduate University for Advanced Studies (Japan)|Graduate University for Advanced Studies]] in [[Hayama]]. In 2009, he transitioned to a three-way appointment as an [[emeritus professor]] at the National Institute for Basic Biology and at the [[Graduate University for Advanced Studies (Japan)|Graduate University for Advanced Studies]], and a professorship at the Advanced Research Organization, Integrated Research Institute, [[Tokyo Institute of Technology]] (Tokyo Tech). After his retirement in 2014, he continued to serve as Professor at Institute of Innovative Research, Tokyo Institute of Technology. Currently, he is head of the Cell Biology Research Unit, Institute of Innovative Research, Tokyo Institute of Technology.<ref name=titech>{{cite web|title=Yoshinori Ohsumi Biography|url=http://www.ohsumilab.aro.iri.titech.ac.jp/ohsumieng.html|publisher=Institute of Innovative Research, Tokyo Institute of Technology|access-date=October 10, 2016|archive-date=October 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161007182221/http://www.ohsumilab.aro.iri.titech.ac.jp/ohsumieng.html}}</ref>

[[Christian de Duve]] coined the term [[autophagy]] in 1963 whereas Ohsumi began his work in 1988. Prior to that time, less than 20 papers per year were published on this subject.<ref name=MoleCluesTV>{{cite web|title=Yoshinori Ohsumi: What is autophagy? A dynamic cellular recycling process|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6bAkvnvX0W8|publisher=Molecular Frontiers Symposium at the Tokyo Institute of Technology, Japan|date=October 2017|access-date=January 15, 2018}}</ref> During the 1990s, Ohsumi's group described the morphology of autophagy in yeast, and performed mutational screening on yeast cells that identified essential genes for cells to be capable of autophagy.<ref>{{cite Q|Q57407776}}</ref><ref>{{cite Q|Q29614174}}</ref>

In 2016, he was awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine]] "for his discoveries of mechanisms for [[autophagy]]".<ref name="Nobel">{{cite web|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/medicine/laureates/2016/ohsumi-lecture.html|title=Yoshinori Ohsumi – Nobel Lecture: Autophagy – an Intracellular Recycling System|date=December 7, 2016|work=[[Nobel Prize]]|access-date=January 15, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Kolata|first1=Gina|last2=Chan|first2=Sewell|title=Yoshinori Ohsumi of Japan Wins Nobel Prize for Study of 'Self-Eating' Cells|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/10/04/science/yoshinori-ohsumi-nobel-prize-medicine.html|access-date=October 10, 2016|work=The New York Times|date=October 3, 2016}}</ref> He is the 25th Japanese person to be awarded a Nobel Prize.<ref name="japantimes">{{cite news|last1=Wanklyn|first1=Alastair|title=Japanese microbiologist Yoshinori Ohsumi wins Nobel in medicine for autophagy research|url=http://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2016/10/03/world/japanese-microbiologist-yoshinori-ohsumi-wins-nobel-prize-in-medicine-for-autophagy-research/|access-date=October 8, 2016|work=[[The Japan Times]]|date=October 3, 2016}}</ref> Ohsumi's spouse Mariko, a Professor at [[Teikyo University of Science]], collaborated on his research.<ref>{{cite web |title=大隅萬里子教授の共同研究がノーベル医学・生理学賞として選定されました |trans-title=A joint research of Professor Mariko Ohsumi won Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine |date=October 5, 2016 |publisher=Teikyo University of Science |url=http://www.ntu.ac.jp/topics/news/2016/10/05201411.html |access-date=October 9, 2016 |archive-date=February 22, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170222063438/http://www.ntu.ac.jp/topics/news/2016/10/05201411.html }}</ref> She is a co-author of many academic papers with him.<ref>{{cite web |title=Google Scholar |url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Yoshinori+Ohsumi%22+%22mariko+Ohsumi%22&btnG=&hl=en&as_sdt=0%2C5|website=Scholar.google.com}}</ref> In 2024 Ohsumi donated his [[Nobel Prize medal]] and diploma to the [[Institute of Science Tokyo]] to "serve as a strong stimulus for young researchers who seek to create the future".<ref name=TTNApr24>{{cite news|url=https://www.titech.ac.jp/english/news/2024/068945|archive-url=|title=Honorary Professor Yoshinori Ohsumi donates Nobel Prize medal to Tokyo Tech|date=12 February 2019|work=[[Institute of Science Tokyo]]|accessdate=17 January 2026|archivedate=}}</ref>
